name: granite_devsquad_v9
description: v9 end-to-end test: review-gate fail-safe (unknown=FAIL), state-exchange FK fix, picoclaw directory-read fix.
objective: Build a simple Flask calculator web application with add, subtract, multiply, divide operations and an HTML frontend. The app must use Flask with render_template for the UI. Test the app thoroughly, prepare deployment artifacts (Dockerfile using python:3.11-slim base image), and deploy it.

members.responsibilities:
Create a Flask calculator web app. Produce these files in /workspace:
- app.py: Flask app with routes /add, /subtract, /multiply, /divide (accepting query params a and b, returning JSON {"result": value}), plus a root route / serving an HTML calculator UI via render_template.
- templates/index.html: Clean HTML/CSS calculator form that posts to the operation routes and displays results.
- requirements.txt: containing flask.
Execute the app briefly with `python3 app.py &` then curl each endpoint to verify it works. Kill the server when done.

Test the Flask calculator app created by the Developer.
1. First check /workspace for REVIEW_BRIEF.md and CEREMONY_PLAN.md to understand what was built.
2. Read the actual app.py to understand the routes and expected behavior.
3. Install flask from requirements.txt if needed.
4. Write test_app.py that imports the Flask app from app.py, creates a test client using app.test_client(), and tests all four operations with known inputs.
5. Run the tests with python3 test_app.py.
6. CRITICAL: You MUST write a file called REVIEW_VERDICT.md in /workspace. The FIRST LINE of this file must be exactly PASS or FAIL (nothing else on that line). If tests passed write PASS on line 1, then details below. If tests failed write FAIL on line 1, then what broke below.
Example:
PASS
All 4 operations tested successfully with correct results.

Review the Flask app files in /workspace (app.py, templates/, requirements.txt).
1. List the workspace contents with: ls -la /workspace
2. Read REVIEW_BRIEF.md if present.
3. Read app.py and requirements.txt to understand the app.
4. Create a Dockerfile using python:3.11-slim as base image, that copies the app files, runs pip install -r requirements.txt, exposes port 5000, and uses CMD ["python3", "app.py"].
5. Create run.sh startup script.
6. Create README.md with build and run instructions.
7. Verify the project structure with ls -laR /workspace.

You have ONE job: look at the workspace, verify that Dockerfile and app.py exist, then emit EXACTLY this line in your response:
DEPLOYMENT_REQUEST:flask-calculator:5000:python3 app.py
Do NOT wrap it in markdown, do NOT add asterisks or backticks. Just print that exact line on its own.

ceremonies.name: Development Review
ceremonies.description: Collect the Developer output (app.py, templates, requirements.txt) and write REVIEW_BRIEF.md so the Tester can see exactly what was built.

ceremonies.name: Test Quality Gate
ceremonies.description: Read the Tester verdict from REVIEW_VERDICT.md. If FAIL, send feedback back to the Developer for rework. If PASS, proceed to DevOps.

ceremonies.name: Final Aggregation
ceremonies.description: Aggregate all agent outputs into FINAL_SUMMARY.md before the Deployer runs.
